title: Aurora: A Child's Journey
description: 3C, Act II gameplay and puzzle design on an award-winning narrative adventure at Luski Game Studio.

blocks.html: Luski Game Studio · 6 team
3D Puzzle / Narrative Adventure
Recognition: Games for Change Latin America 2020 — Winner · BIG Festival Impact 2021 — Finalist. Released on Steam.
Character movement and camera responsiveness must achieve absolute mechanical precision before layout challenges can be introduced fairly.
An all-ages story teaches through space, motion and discovery rather than text and tutorials.
Puzzles escalate from intuition to insight without punishing failure. Curiosity is always rewarded.

blocks.text: What I owned, and where the team came in

blocks.html:
• Act II gameplay and puzzle design, end-to-end
  • 3C tuning: camera framing and control feel
  • Playtest plans, sessions and synthesis
  • Puzzle pacing and difficulty progression

• 3C implementation: with programming
  • Blockout and level flow: with level design
  • Narrative and art direction: with the team
  • Audio and mood: with the wider studio

In a narrative adventure, feel is the first impression. Before a puzzle can be fair or a story can land, the player has to trust how the character moves and how the camera reads space. I co-developed the 3C around clarity and comfort for all ages.

The camera is the player's narrator: it should reveal the puzzle, not fight it.

  • Framing that hints at the next goal
  • Smooth, predictable follow, no motion sickness
  • Composed angles for story beats

To accommodate an all-ages demographic, input detection must be forgiving and intuitive, so player intent translates seamlessly into action.

  • Responsive input with gentle assists
  • Readable animation that telegraphs state
  • Fine-tuned jump and interaction tolerances

Generous interaction and collision thresholds mean failure reads as a learning loop rather than mechanical friction.
I owned the gameplay for the entire second act, designing puzzles and partnering with level design to refine blockout and flow so each space teaches the player something new.

Environmental layouts introduce mechanics in isolated, safe environments before combining them, eliminating the need for text-based tutorials. Each mechanic is introduced safely, practiced, combined with prior ideas, then mastered for an earned "aha" — the space is the lesson.
A progression curve based on intuition-to-insight leaps, with soft fail-states and rapid retry loops that encourage experimentation over punishment.

• Iterated layouts for readability and pacing
  • Sightlines that guide without hand-holding
  • A rhythm of tension and calm across the act

• Gameplay paced to support story moments
  • Quiet spaces between challenges to breathe
  • Emotional payoff tied to puzzle resolution
For an all-ages adventure, playtesting is everything: what reads as obvious to a designer can stump a first-time player. One representative loop from Act II — observe, change, measure.

Playtest data highlighted a critical affordance failure in an Act II puzzle sequence. Players consistently missed a key interaction node, leading to progression dead-ends, loss of narrative momentum and early session abandonment.

Reframed the camera hierarchy to highlight the puzzle objective, adjusted blockout sightlines together with Level Design, and integrated organic environmental lighting cues to guide the player without hand-holding.

items.label: of playtesters solved it, after the change

blocks.html: Puzzle resolution rates rose to around 90% across subsequent playtest cohorts, preserving the intended "aha!" moment while restoring narrative pacing.
Happy to walk through the design documentation and tuning decisions behind this project.
